# 303box

> 303box is a browser-based 16-step pattern sketchpad for writing, previewing and transferring 303 acid bassline and rhythm ideas to hardware.

Canonical URL: https://303box.com/
Turkish landing page: https://303box.com/tr/

## Important positioning
- 303box is not an AI composition service.
- 303box is not intended to replace a musician, live performance, hardware performance or final recording decisions.
- Pattern Random uses explicit rule-based randomization; it provides an editable starting sketch rather than finished AI-generated music.
- The main purpose is convenience: make 16-step note/rhythm entry easier to read and edit than working only through a small hardware interface.
- The user decides which notes, rests, accents, slides, rhythms and sound settings remain in the pattern.
- Browser audio is an audition/preview surface for the sketch.
- MIDI can help move the sketch to compatible hardware; final sound shaping, performance and hardware WRITE/save remain with the user/device.
- The software development process has included AI-assisted coding, but the musical pattern engine itself is not an AI composition model.

## Core capabilities
- Program 16-step 303 patterns with note, octave, accent, slide, trigger, tie and rest states.
- Choose sawtooth or square waveform for the browser preview and shape Tune, Cutoff, Resonance, Env Mod, Decay and Accent.
- Preview bass and rhythm with the Web Audio API.
- Run bass and rhythm from one shared browser audio clock through the Acid Console.
- Control Master, 303 and Rhythm levels independently.
- Apply shared Swing and Pump behavior.
- Inspect the browser bass signal with Scope and FFT views.
- Connect compatible MIDI hardware through Web MIDI and send notes plus optional clock/transport.
- Use device routing profiles for Roland T-8, Behringer TD-3 / TD-3-MO, Korg volca bass / nubass and Generic MIDI.
- Use the T-8 REC helper to perform a live MIDI pass after REC is armed on the hardware; final WRITE/save remains on the physical device.
- Program a synchronized six-part rhythm sketch: bass drum, snare, clap, tom, closed hi-hat and open hi-hat.
- Generate rule-based acid and rhythm starting patterns that remain fully editable.
- Export visible 303 and rhythm patterns as image references.
- Store working sessions locally in the browser.

- online 303 pattern editor
- 303 pattern sketchpad
- hardware 303 pattern workflow

## Historical coverage
The site includes 303 history and educational coverage of acid-house sequencing culture, including the role of hands-on experimentation and the continuing hardware/software ecosystem.
